extra.reason: Completed research and written comprehensive documentation in ./docs/

Merged e61c003 (branch worktree-agent-a6718f49c5aa7fdcd, commit 29ad489). Go server skeleton: single origin (no subdomain/Host routing — verified by smoke test, a foreign Host header still gets 200), SQLite store with numbered migrations, static PWA serving via web/embed.go, /healthz + /readyz. go build/vet/test clean, CGO_ENABLED=0 static binary. Deferred and re-filed: rate_limit.go NOT ported (its constants are ceremonyRateLimit* and A1 has no ceremony endpoints — a limiter wrapping nothing is dead code plus a background ticker); A3 ports it near-verbatim, and the X-Forwarded-For clientIP handling there is load-bearing. accounts table deliberately minimal (id, created_at_unix) — A3/A5 hang their tables off it.

Merged e61c003 (commit 29ad489). crypto.js ported to mp/v1 labels with salt_kek = SHA-256('myportfolio/v1/prf-kek'). Dropped per spec: oplog record crypto, push payload, MCP frame, X25519 inbox. Added encryptState/decryptState. 51/51 node --test, vectors pinned in vectors.json — and the executor mutation-checked them (flipping mp/v1/data and the state-version framing each fail the suite), so the pins genuinely bite rather than just being green. Tests are .mjs so they load as ESM regardless of package.json scope; verified 51/51 in all three scoping worlds. Resolved a spec gap: state AAD version framing is fixed 8-byte big-endian and means the version the blob WILL be stored as — now pinned in ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (335ef7f) as a wire contract A5/A6 must honour.

Merged 3ddb2fd (branch worktree-agent-a0cd37dd82a8055fe, commits 196b12b/dee1881/f296415). The §3 records port over Dexie, §4 schema, §5 fixed-point money. Reviewed in depth: parseFixed parses digit-wise and never touches parseFloat; products go through BigInt and narrow only via a safe-integer check so precision loss throws instead of silently truncating; rounding is half-away-from-zero and consistent across the parse and divide paths including negatives; proportion(c,h,h)===c exactly, so closing a position leaves no basis dust. The port owns recordId/recordType/clientTs/deleted structurally via spread order, del writes a tombstone, and records.js holds no Dexie import so the rules test under plain Node. Codex found three real bugs, all confirmed empirically before fixing: non-positive shares built a short with positive basis; unpadded MM-DD keys won the latest-close race as strings; toFixed rounds the binary value and lost a cent on 1.005. Accepted web/package.json ({type:module}) as a necessary deviation — Node 18.19 cannot import ESM from .js without it; flagged by the executor rather than buried.

Merged 3ddb2fd. portfolio.js: folds the transaction log into positions, moving-average cost basis, realized/unrealized P/L, account balances, chunked-price valuation, asOf. Every §4 transaction type handled; oversell surfaced as an issue rather than clamped; mixed currencies raise currency_not_converted once per currency rather than silently summing unlike units. Fee/tax divergence (fees capitalise into basis, taxes never do) confirmed as intended and promoted into ARCHITECTURE.md §4 in 335ef7f, since it changes every realized-gain number. FIFO/LIFO deferred with a ponytail: comment naming the upgrade path. 51/51 node --test at merge; 102/102 across both tracks on the merged tree.

Merged (branch worktree-agent-a7d2bc010400b1d86, commits 679d12e + 1ecf31f). Ported the --wg-* token system, both self-hosted font families, 10 domain-neutral primitives, the shared modal/toolbar/field utilities, and 6 guard tests. 230/230 on the merged tree; clean merge with no conflicts.

Verified independently rather than trusting the report: injected a hardcoded hex and it failed 'no hardcoded hex colors outside :root'; deleted the gain glyph rule and it failed 'every delta modifier emits a sign glyph — gain/loss is never encoded by color alone'. The guards bite.

Best call in this bead: the gain/loss accessibility requirement was implemented STRUCTURALLY, not as a convention. .wg-delta--gain/loss/flat::before emits the glyph from CSS and a test fails if it is removed, so a screens author cannot forget it and a future cleanup cannot silently delete it. That is stronger than what was asked for.

Close judgment calls, all sound: wg-ring kept (generic gauge) but wg-ring-stack dropped (its accent tokens were medication-domain); wg-icons trimmed of pill/apple/dumbbell/etc and given layers+list for Holdings/Transactions; --tg-theme-* dropped but the legacy colour NAMES kept as aliases onto the wg palette so ported utility blocks carried over byte-identical.

Two guards deliberately widened beyond the sibling and now recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md §9: inline-styles covers every file with an EMPTY allowlist (no legacy to grandfather), and no-external-fonts covers every .html and .css plus asserts the named woff2 files exist. Both will bite future frontend executors, by design.

Deferred with reasons: WGStaleBadge.mountFromKey (was bound to the sibling's ApiCache; render/formatLabel came over pure). domain-purity and sw-precache guards have nothing to bind to until the shell exists — moved to g7e.6. action-row.js kept verbatim including its emoji, flagged for later migration to the icon registry.

Merged via PR #1 (branch b3-perf-engine). TTWROR + IRR in web/domain/perf.js; consumes portfolio.js snapshot({asOf}), never re-derives positions. 247/247 at merge.

Verified the headline claim independently rather than trusting it: ran my own bisection on Microsoft's XIRR example and the true root is 0.373362533519. The engine lands 1.9e-11 away; Excel's published 0.373362535 is 1.5e-09 away, and NPV at the published figure is -8.6e-6 versus ~zero at the engine's. The executor chased a 4e-9 discrepancy instead of widening the tolerance to make its test pass — the right instinct in a returns engine. Also checked the multi-root fixture algebraically: -1000x^2+2500x-1540 does factor at exactly 1.1 and 1.4.

Deviated from the bead deliberately and correctly: bracket-and-bisect with no Newton step. Newton's failure modes here all return confident wrong numbers and the repair for each is the bracket the fallback must build anyway — less code and no silent-garbage path. Non-convergence returns an explicit result carrying no 'value', so a caller cannot accidentally render a number.

TTWROR breaks at every flow day AND the day before it; that second boundary is what makes a mid-period deposit not move the result, and it is directly tested against the distorted 27.27% figure.

Codex: one finding dismissed after actually running it (excluding transfers as 'internal' prints a phantom -40%, because portfolio.js really does report the total dropping while a transfer is in flight) — both directions now regression tests. One finding fixed and real: same-day matched transfer legs applied gross diluted a 10% day to 9.09%; flows now net per day.
